sections.html: Auchenoglanis wittei is a very peaceful and attractive catfish. It reaches a length of at least about 30 cm.
Keep in mind that this catfish attains at least about 30 cm, so it is suited only for large aquaria in the long term. Juvenile imports are currently 5-7 cm long.
In the Congo the genus is represented by Auchenoglanis wittei. The true A. occidentalis occurs in the Senegal, Casamance and Gambia rivers and is not imported as an aquarium fish.

Until recently only two species of Auchenoglanis were commonly accepted, namely A. biscutatus and A. occidentalis. This changed with the revision of Retzer (2010), who recognizes eight different species. A. wittei can be easily identified by the "reticulated giraffe" pattern of the body. It is the species most commonly referred to as A. occidentalis in aquarium literature (the real A. occidentalis is spotted as a juvenile and uniformly brown as an adult). It will probably take a long time until the correct determination is known by hobbyists.
